
# How to Send and Receive Text Messages: Complete Beginner's Guide


## What is this in plain English?


Remember when the only way to send a quick written message to someone was to mail a letter—which took days to arrive—or send a telegram, which was expensive and reserved for urgent news? Casual, everyday written communication meant picking up the phone and calling, which required both people to be available at the same moment and interrupted whatever they were doing. If you wanted to tell someone "Running 10 minutes late" or "Pick up milk on your way home," you had to hope they were near a phone, have an awkward conversation with whoever answered, or accept that they simply wouldn't know until you arrived.


Text messaging—sending short written messages instantly through your phone—revolutionized communication so completely that it's now the primary way billions of people stay in touch. Unlike phone calls, text messages are asynchronous (you send when convenient, they read when convenient—no scheduling required), silent (won't disturb meetings or sleeping babies), written (creates a record you can reference later), and nearly universal (works on any phone, any carrier, anywhere in the world). You can have dozens of ongoing conversations simultaneously, send a quick thought without the commitment of a full phone call, share photos and links instantly, and communicate with people whose language you don't speak using translation apps.


Yet for people who didn't grow up with phones in their hands—especially those who got their first cell phone as adults—text messaging can feel intimidating, confusing, or unnecessarily complicated. The interface seems different from anything they've used before. Abbreviations and acronyms (LOL, BRB, TTYL) look like a foreign language. The etiquette is unclear: Is it rude to text instead of calling? How quickly should you respond? What if you make a typo? These anxieties prevent many people from using what is genuinely the easiest, most convenient form of communication ever invented.


This guide teaches you everything: what text messaging is and how it works, the difference between SMS, MMS, and messaging apps, how to send your first text message step-by-step, how to receive and reply to texts, how to send photos and other media, understanding group chats, text message etiquette, common abbreviations and emoji, troubleshooting when messages don't send, and staying safe with text messages. Whether you've never sent a text or you text occasionally but want to feel more confident, this guide explains everything with patience, clarity, and zero judgment.


## Before You Start: Understanding Text Messages


**What Is a Text Message?**


A text message (also called SMS or texting) is a short written message sent from one phone to another using cellular networks. Unlike email (which requires internet) or phone calls (which require both people available simultaneously), text messages:

- Send instantly (usually delivered within seconds)
- Don't require internet connection (use cellular network like phone calls)
- Work between any phones (iPhone to Android, old flip phone to smartphone—all compatible)
- Can be read anytime (recipient reads when convenient)
- Create written record (messages saved in conversation history)
- Are silent (don't ring or disturb recipient)

**Types of Text Messages:**


**SMS (Short Message Service):**

- Text-only messages
- Original text messaging format (from 1990s)
- Limited to 160 characters per message
- Works on all phones (even old ones)
- Sent over cellular network (not internet)

**MMS (Multimedia Messaging Service):**

- Text + photos, videos, audio, or emoji
- No character limit
- Requires compatible phone (most smartphones)
- Uses cellular data (may cost more on some plans)

**Modern smartphones automatically choose:**

- SMS for plain text
- MMS when you add photo, emoji, or long message
- You don't need to think about the difference—phone handles it

**Messaging Apps (Different from SMS/MMS):**


Some apps use internet instead of cellular networks:


| App                                   | How It Works                         | Need to Know                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **iMessage**                          | Apple's messaging (iPhone to iPhone) | Automatically used when both people have iPhones; shows as blue bubbles; uses WiFi or data instead of cellular |
| **WhatsApp**                          | Internet-based messaging app         | Both people must have WhatsApp installed; works internationally for free                                       |
| **Facebook Messenger**                | Facebook's messaging                 | Requires Facebook account; separate from SMS                                                                   |
| **RCS** (Rich Communication Services) | Enhanced SMS (Android)               | New standard—adds features like read receipts and typing indicators                                            |


**This guide focuses on standard SMS/MMS** (the basic text messaging everyone has, regardless of phone type).


**What You Need to Send Text Messages:**


**Essential:**

- Cell phone (smartphone or basic phone)
- Active cellular service (phone plan with carrier: AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, etc.)
- Recipient's phone number

**Not required:**

- Internet connection (SMS/MMS use cellular network)
- Smartphone (basic flip phones can text—though smartphone is easier)
- Same type of phone as recipient (iPhone texts to Android and vice versa)

**Text Messaging Plans:**


**Most modern phone plans include:**

- Unlimited texting (send/receive as many as you want)
- Unlimited picture messages (MMS)
- No per-message charges

**If you have older plan:**

- Check with carrier about texting limits
- Some charge per message (rare now)
- Unlimited texting typically costs $5-20/month if not included

**Group Texts vs. Individual Texts:**


**Individual (one-to-one):**

- Private conversation between you and one other person
- Only you two see messages

**Group text:**

- One message sent to multiple people simultaneously
- Everyone in group sees all replies
- Useful for coordinating plans, family updates, etc.

## Step 1: Finding and Opening Your Messaging App


**Every phone has a messaging app pre-installed—you just need to locate it.**


**iPhone:**


**Messages app icon:**

- Green icon with white speech bubble
- Usually on home screen (main screen when you unlock phone)
- Often located in dock (bottom row that stays visible on all screens)

**If you can't find it:**

1. Swipe down from middle of home screen (opens search)
2. Type "Messages"
3. App appears in search results
4. Tap to open

**Android:**


**Messages app icon varies by phone manufacturer:**

- **Google Messages:** Speech bubble icon (usually blue, green, or white)
- **Samsung Messages:** Speech bubble (often green)
- Text may say "Messages" or "Messaging"

**Common locations:**

- Home screen
- App drawer (swipe up from bottom of screen to see all apps)

**If you can't find it:**

1. Open app drawer (swipe up)
2. Look for "Messages" or "Messaging"
3. OR tap search icon, type "messages"

**What the App Looks Like When Opened:**


**iPhone Messages app:**

- List of conversations (recent texts at top)
- Each conversation shows:
    - Contact name or phone number
    - Preview of last message
    - Time of last message
- Blue "New Message" button (top-right corner) to start new conversation
- Search bar at top to find specific conversation

**Android Messages app:**

- Similar layout (conversation list)
- "+" or "Start chat" button (bottom-right corner usually) to start new conversation
- Search icon at top

**If list is empty:** You haven't sent or received any texts yet (completely normal for new users).


## Step 2: Sending Your First Text Message


**Let's send a simple text message step-by-step.**


**iPhone Instructions:**


**1. Open Messages app** (green icon with white speech bubble)


**2. Tap "New Message" button:**

- Blue circular button with pencil icon (top-right corner)
- OR tap pencil/compose icon

**3. Choose recipient:**


**Option A: Select from contacts:**

- Tap "To:" field at top
- Start typing contact's name
- Contact appears below as you type
- Tap their name when it appears

**Option B: Enter phone number manually:**

- Tap "To:" field
- Type phone number
- Include area code (example: 555-123-4567)
- Don't worry about formatting (hyphens optional—phone adds them)

**4. Type your message:**

- Tap large text field at bottom (says "iMessage" or "Text Message")
- Keyboard appears
- Type your message
    - Example: "Hi! This is my first text message."
    - OR simple: "Hello"

**5. Send:**

- Tap blue up-arrow button (right side of text field)
- Message sends immediately
- Appears in conversation as blue bubble (iMessage) or green bubble (SMS)

**Android Instructions:**


**1. Open Messages app**


**2. Tap "New message" or "+" button:**

- Usually floating button bottom-right corner
- OR "Start chat" button

**3. Choose recipient:**


**From contacts:**

- Tap "To" field
- Start typing name
- Select contact when it appears

**Manual phone number:**

- Type phone number in "To" field
- Include area code

**4. Type message:**

- Tap "Text message" field at bottom
- Keyboard appears
- Type your message

**5. Send:**

- Tap send button (paper airplane icon or arrow)
- Message sends
- Appears in conversation

**What Happens After You Send:**


**Message status indicators:**


**iPhone:**

- **Blue bubble:** iMessage (sent to another iPhone via internet)
- **Green bubble:** SMS/MMS (sent via cellular network)
- **"Delivered"** appears below message (means it reached their phone)
- **"Read"** may appear (if read receipts enabled—means they opened it)

**Android:**

- Message appears in conversation
- **Single checkmark:** Sent from your phone
- **Double checkmark:** Delivered to their phone
- **Blue checkmarks:** Read (if RCS enabled)

**Delivery time:**

- Usually instant (within seconds)
- Occasionally delayed (poor signal, recipient's phone off)
- If stuck "Sending..." for minutes, see troubleshooting section

## Step 3: Receiving and Reading Text Messages


**When someone sends you a text, your phone notifies you automatically.**


**How You Know You Received a Text:**


**Notifications:**


**iPhone:**

- **Sound:** Ding or chime (default text message sound)
- **Screen notification:** Banner appears at top showing sender and preview
- **Lock screen:** Notification appears even when phone locked
- **Badge:** Red number appears on Messages app icon (shows unread count)

**Android:**

- **Sound:** Notification tone
- **Banner:** Appears at top of screen
- **Lock screen:** Shows notification
- **Badge/dot:** Indicator on Messages app icon

**Opening and Reading a Text:**


**From notification:**

- **Tap notification** when it appears
- Opens directly to that conversation
- Can read and reply immediately

**From Messages app:**

1. Open Messages app
2. **Conversation list** shows all texts
3. **Unread conversations** appear in bold or with blue dot
4. **Tap conversation** to open
5. All messages in that conversation appear (newest at bottom)
6. Scroll up to see older messages

**Reading the Conversation:**


**How messages display:**

- **Your messages:** Appear on right side (blue or green bubbles on iPhone, colored bubbles on Android)
- **Their messages:** Appear on left side (gray bubbles usually)
- **Timestamps:** Show when messages were sent (tap message to see exact time)
- **Photos/media:** Display inline (tap to view full-size)

**Scrolling through conversation:**

- Swipe up to see older messages
- Swipe down to return to recent messages

**Managing Notifications:**


**If notifications too frequent or distracting:**


**iPhone:**

- Settings → Notifications → Messages
- Customize:
    - Allow Notifications: ON/OFF
    - Sounds: Choose sound or silent
    - Badges: ON/OFF (red number on icon)
    - Show Previews: Always, When Unlocked, or Never (privacy)

**Android:**

- Settings → Apps → Messages → Notifications
- Adjust sound, vibration, pop-up, preview settings

**Do Not Disturb mode:**

- Silences all notifications during set times (nighttime, meetings)
- iPhone: Settings → Focus → Do Not Disturb
- Android: Settings → Sound → Do Not Disturb

## Step 4: Replying to Text Messages


**Responding to a received text.**


**Opening the Conversation:**


**From notification:**

- Tap notification banner (quickest way)
- Opens conversation, keyboard ready

**From Messages app:**

- Open app
- Tap conversation
- Keyboard appears at bottom

**Typing Your Reply:**


**1. Tap text field** (bottom of screen)

- Keyboard appears
- Cursor blinks in text field

**2. Type your message:**

- Use keyboard like any typing
- Corrections: Tap backspace to delete (← key)
- Autocorrect: Phone suggests words—tap space to accept, ignore to keep what you typed

**3. Review message:**

- Read before sending
- Fix typos if needed
- Don't worry about perfection—casual texts often have minor errors

**4. Send:**

- Tap send button (up-arrow or paper airplane icon)
- Message appears in conversation
- Keyboard remains open for continued conversation

**Continuing the Conversation:**


**Back-and-forth texting:**

- Type reply → Send
- Read their response
- Reply again
- Continue as long as you want

**No need to:**

- Say goodbye formally (texts are informal)
- Wait for response before doing something else (can put phone down, they'll reply when ready)
- Match their response speed (reply when convenient for you)

**Exiting the Conversation:**


**To leave conversation without closing:**

- Simply stop replying
- No formal ending needed for texts
- Can resume anytime

**To close Messages app:**

- **iPhone:** Swipe up from bottom of screen (or press home button)
- **Android:** Tap back button or home button

**Conversation stays in Messages app**—can return to it anytime.


## Step 5: Sending Photos, Emoji, and Other Media


**Text messages can include more than just text.**


**Sending a Photo:**


**iPhone:**


**1. Open conversation** (or start new message)


**2. Tap camera icon** (left side of text field)

- **Option A: Take new photo:**
    - Tap camera icon
    - Camera opens
    - Take photo
    - Tap "Use Photo"
- **Option B: Choose existing photo:**
    - Tap camera icon
    - Photo library appears
    - Scroll through photos
    - Tap photo to select
    - Can select multiple (tap each one)

**3. Add caption (optional):**

- Type message in text field
- Photo and text send together

**4. Tap send button:**

- Photo sends (may take 5-30 seconds depending on file size)
- Appears in conversation

**Android:**


**1. Open conversation**


**2. Tap attachment icon:**

- Usually "+" or paperclip icon near text field

**3. Choose option:**

- **Camera:** Take new photo
- **Gallery:** Choose from existing photos
- Tap photo to select

**4. Add message (optional)**


**5. Tap send**


**Photo appears in conversation for both you and recipient.**


**Receiving Photos:**


**When someone sends you photo:**

- Appears in conversation
- Tap to view full-size
- Pinch to zoom
- Swipe to close

**Saving received photos:**

- **iPhone:** Tap photo → Share icon → Save Image
- **Android:** Long-press photo → Save or Download

**Using Emoji:**


**Emoji = small pictures expressing emotions, objects, ideas** (😊 ❤️ 👍 🎉)


**iPhone:**


**1. Tap text field** (keyboard appears)


**2. Tap emoji button:**

- Smiley face icon (bottom-left of keyboard)
- Keyboard changes to emoji

**3. Browse emoji:**

- Swipe left/right through categories
- Bottom row shows categories (smileys, animals, food, activities, etc.)
- Tap category icon to jump to that section

**4. Tap emoji to insert:**

- Adds to message
- Can add multiple emoji
- Mix text and emoji in same message: "Great idea! 👍"

**5. Return to text keyboard:**

- Tap "ABC" button (bottom-left)

**Android:**


**Similar process:**

- Tap emoji/smiley icon on keyboard
- Browse and select
- Tap to insert
- Return to text with "ABC" or keyboard icon

**Common emoji meanings:**


| Emoji | Meaning                   |
| ----- | ------------------------- |
| 😊    | Happy, friendly           |
| 👍    | Thumbs up, agree, okay    |
| ❤️    | Love, care                |
| 😂    | Laughing                  |
| 👋    | Hello or goodbye          |
| 🎉    | Celebration               |
| 🙏    | Thank you, prayer, please |
| 😢    | Sad                       |
| 🤔    | Thinking                  |
| ✅     | Confirmed, done           |


**Sending Other Media:**


**Videos:**

- Same process as photos (camera icon → choose video)
- Keep videos short (large files slow to send)

**Voice messages:**

- **iPhone:** Tap microphone icon (hold to record, release to send)
- **Android:** Tap microphone icon (record, tap send)
- Recipient plays audio message

**Location:**

- Share current location or address
- iPhone: Tap "i" icon in conversation → Send My Current Location
- Android: Tap attachment → Location

**Links:**

- Copy link (URL) from browser
- Paste into text message
- Sends as clickable link

## Step 6: Managing Conversations and Contacts


**Organizing your messages and contacts.**


**Deleting Individual Messages:**


**iPhone:**

- Long-press (tap and hold) message bubble
- Menu appears → "More"
- Checkboxes appear next to messages
- Select messages to delete
- Tap trash icon (bottom-left)
- Confirm "Delete Message"

**Android:**

- Long-press message
- Tap delete icon or "Delete" option
- Confirm

**Deleting Entire Conversations:**


**iPhone:**

- Conversation list (main Messages screen)
- Swipe left on conversation
- Tap "Delete"
- OR: Tap "Edit" (top-left) → Select conversations → Delete

**Android:**

- Long-press conversation
- Tap delete icon
- Confirm

**Deleted conversations = permanently removed** (can't be recovered without backup).


**Searching for Old Messages:**


**iPhone:**

- Conversation list → Pull down (search bar appears)
- Type search term (name, word, phrase)
- Results show matching conversations and messages
- Tap result to jump to that message

**Android:**

- Tap search icon (magnifying glass)
- Type search term
- Results appear
- Tap to view

**Adding Someone to Contacts:**


**If you receive text from unknown number:**


**iPhone:**

1. Open conversation with unknown number
2. Tap number at top
3. "Add to Contacts" or "Create New Contact"
4. Enter name
5. Save

**Android:**

1. Tap unknown number
2. "Add contact" or "Create contact"
3. Enter details
4. Save

**Now their name appears instead of number in future texts.**


**Muting Conversations:**


**For group texts or frequent messagers you don't want notifications from:**


**iPhone:**

- Open conversation
- Tap name/number at top
- Toggle "Hide Alerts" ON
- Conversation muted (messages still arrive, no notifications)

**Android:**

- Long-press conversation
- Tap bell icon with slash (mute)
- OR: Open conversation → Menu → Mute notifications

**Blocking Unwanted Numbers:**


**For spam or unwanted contacts:**


**iPhone:**

- Open conversation
- Tap number/name at top
- Scroll down → "Block this Caller"
- Confirm
- They can't text or call you (they're not notified)

**Android:**

- Open conversation
- Menu (⋮) → Block or Details → Block & report spam
- Confirm

**Blocked numbers can be unblocked anytime** (Settings → Messages → Blocked Contacts).


## Step 7: Group Text Messages


**Texting multiple people simultaneously.**


**What Is a Group Text?**


A group text (or group message) is a single conversation with multiple recipients. Everyone in the group:

- Sees all messages sent by anyone
- Can reply to the group (reply-all by default)
- Receives notifications for every message

**Common uses:**

- Family coordination ("What time is dinner?")
- Event planning ("Anyone want to see a movie Friday?")
- Work groups ("Meeting moved to 3pm")
- Friend groups ("Who's coming to the party?")

**Starting a Group Text:**


**iPhone:**


**1. New Message** (compose icon)


**2. Add multiple recipients:**

- Tap "To:" field
- Type first person's name → Select
- Type second person's name → Select
- Continue adding people (up to 20-30 people)
- OR: Tap "+" icon → Select multiple from contacts

**3. Type message:**

- Message goes to entire group

**4. Send:**

- Everyone receives message
- Replies go to entire group

**Android:**


**Similar process:**

- New message
- Add multiple recipients (tap "To:" field, add each person)
- Type message
- Send

**Replying in Group Text:**


**Your reply goes to everyone in group automatically.**

- Open group conversation
- Type reply
- Send
- All group members see your message

**Individual vs. Group Reply:**


**iPhone:**

- Default: Reply goes to entire group
- To message one person individually: Exit group text → Start new conversation with just that person

**Android:**

- Same: Group replies go to all

**No easy "reply to one person" in group text**—must start separate conversation.


**Naming a Group Chat:**


**Makes groups easier to identify:**


**iPhone:**

- Open group conversation
- Tap group icons/numbers at top
- "Enter a Group Name" or tap (i) → "Name"
- Type name (example: "Family," "Book Club," "Softball Team")
- Done
- Group name appears in conversation list

**Android:**

- Open group conversation
- Tap menu (⋮) → Group details
- Tap "Group name"
- Enter name
- Save

**Leaving a Group Text:**


**If group text becomes too active or no longer relevant:**


**iPhone (iMessage group only):**

- Open group conversation
- Tap group at top → Info (i)
- Scroll down → "Leave this Conversation"
- Confirm
- You're removed from group (others aren't notified)

**Note:** Can only leave iMessage groups (blue bubbles—all iPhones). Can't leave SMS/MMS groups (green bubbles—mixed phone types).


**Android (RCS group):**

- Similar option in group settings
- Exit or leave group

**SMS/MMS groups (green bubbles):**

- Can't officially leave
- Must mute notifications or ask group creator to remove you

**Muting Group Texts:**


**If leaving isn't possible but group is too active:**

- Open group conversation
- Mute notifications (see Step 6)
- Messages still arrive, but you're not notified

## Step 8: Text Message Etiquette


**Unwritten rules of polite texting.**


**When to Text vs. Call:**


**Text is appropriate for:**

- Quick questions or updates ("Running late")
- Non-urgent communication
- Sharing information (address, link, photo)
- When recipient might be busy (can read and respond later)
- Group coordination
- Follow-up after phone conversation (sending info discussed)

**Call is more appropriate for:**

- Urgent matters
- Complex conversations requiring back-and-forth
- Emotional or sensitive topics
- Elderly relatives or others who prefer calls
- Emergency situations

**Both are fine—choose based on situation and recipient's preference.**


**Response Time Expectations:**


**No universal rule, but general guidelines:**

- **Immediate response not expected** (that's the point of texting—read when convenient)
- **Within a few hours:** Polite for non-urgent messages
- **Same day:** Generally acceptable
- **Next day:** Fine for casual conversations
- **Longer delays:** May need explanation ("Sorry for delay, busy week")

**Urgency indicators:**

- If truly urgent, call instead
- Can text first: "Call me when you have a minute, it's urgent"

**Don't stress about "perfect" response time**—texts are asynchronous communication.


**Group Text Etiquette:**


**Be considerate:**

- Don't add people to groups without asking (especially large groups)
- Stay on topic (don't derail group conversation)
- Consider individual replies for side conversations
- Mute if group becomes too active for you
- Reply strategically (not every message needs response from everyone)

**Avoid:**

- Sending dozens of messages in row (consolidate thoughts)
- Very early morning or late night messages (unless you know person's schedule)

**Texting Strangers or Professional Contacts:**


**More formal than friends/family:**

- Introduce yourself if they don't have your number ("Hi, this is John from accounting")
- Be clear and concise
- Avoid excessive emoji or abbreviations
- Proofread before sending
- Respect business hours

**Reading Receipts and Typing Indicators:**


**Some platforms show when:**

- Message was read ("Read" receipt)
- Other person is typing ("..." appears)

**This can feel like pressure:**

- You're not obligated to respond immediately just because they know you read it
- Can disable read receipts if uncomfortable:
    - iPhone: Settings → Messages → Send Read Receipts → OFF
    - Android: Messages settings → Read receipts → OFF

**Typos and Autocorrect:**


**Don't stress about minor typos:**

- Texts are informal—people understand
- Major typo: Send correction ("*their" to fix "there")
- OR: Send follow-up message: "I meant..."

**Autocorrect mistakes:**

- Common and often funny
- Usually obvious from context
- Correct if meaning unclear, otherwise continue

**Length of Messages:**


**No strict rules, but:**

- Short and frequent messages common for casual chat
- Longer messages fine for updates or explanations
- Very long messages (multiple paragraphs): Consider calling or emailing instead
- Break very long thoughts into 2-3 messages for readability

**Abbreviations and Slang:**


**Common with younger texters:**

- LOL (laughing out loud)
- BRB (be right back)
- OMG (oh my god)
- TBH (to be honest)
- IDK (I don't know)

**Not required:**

- Type full words if more comfortable
- Recipient will understand either way

## Step 9: Common Abbreviations and Emoji


**Understanding text message shorthand.**


**Common Abbreviations:**


| Abbreviation   | Meaning                              | Example Usage             |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------- |
| **LOL**        | Laughing out loud                    | "That's so funny LOL"     |
| **OMG**        | Oh my god                            | "OMG I can't believe it"  |

**You don't need to use these**—full words work perfectly fine.

## Step 10: Troubleshooting Common Problems


**When Things Don't Work:**


**Problem: Message Won't Send**


**Shows "Not Delivered" or stuck "Sending...":**


**Causes and solutions:**


**1. Poor cellular signal:**

- Check signal bars (top-left corner)
- If low/no signal, move to area with better reception
- Try sending again when signal improves

**2. Airplane mode accidentally on:**

- Check for airplane icon in status bar
- Settings → Airplane Mode → OFF (or swipe down, tap airplane icon)

**3. Recipient's phone off or out of service:**

- Message sends when their phone reconnects
- Nothing you can do—wait

**4. Message blocked by carrier:**

- Very long messages sometimes fail
- Try breaking into shorter messages

**5. Restart phone:**

- Turn off completely
- Wait 30 seconds
- Turn back on
- Try sending again

**Problem: Not Receiving Messages**


**Someone says they texted, but you didn't get it:**


**1. Check blocked list:**

- Sender might be accidentally blocked
- Settings → Messages → Blocked Contacts (iPhone)
- Unblock if needed

**2. Check storage:**

- Phone storage full can prevent receiving messages
- Settings → General → iPhone Storage (check available space)
- Delete apps or photos if storage critically low

**3. Restart phone** (fixes many issues)


**4. Update phone:**

- Settings → General → Software Update
- Install if update available

**Problem: Green Bubbles vs. Blue Bubbles (iPhone)**


**iPhone users may notice:**

- **Blue bubbles:** iMessage (to other iPhones)
- **Green bubbles:** SMS/MMS (to Android or when iMessage unavailable)

**Why this matters:**

- Blue (iMessage): Uses WiFi/data, free, more features
- Green (SMS): Uses cellular network, may count toward text limits on old plans

**If expecting blue but seeing green:**

- Recipient doesn't have iPhone
- Recipient has iMessage turned off
- No internet connection (fell back to SMS)
- Nothing wrong—message still sends

**Problem: Can't Send Photos**


**MMS not working:**


**1. Check MMS is enabled:**

- Settings → Messages → MMS Messaging → ON (iPhone)
- Settings → Apps → Messages → Advanced → MMS → Enable (Android)

**2. Cellular data must be on:**

- MMS requires data connection
- Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data → ON

**3. Photo too large:**

- Compress or choose smaller photo
- Some carriers limit MMS size

**Problem: Duplicate Messages**


**Receiving same message multiple times:**

- Usually carrier issue (temporary)
- Resolves on its own
- If persistent, contact carrier support

**Problem: Wrong Date/Time on Messages:**


**Messages showing incorrect timestamp:**


**1. Check phone time settings:**

- Settings → General → Date & Time
- Enable "Set Automatically"

**2. Restart phone**


**Problem: Notifications Not Working:**


**Not receiving notification sounds/alerts:**


**1. Check notification settings:**

- Settings → Notifications → Messages
- Allow Notifications → ON
- Sounds → Select sound (not "None")

**2. Check Do Not Disturb:**

- May be silencing notifications
- Settings → Focus → Do Not Disturb → OFF

**3. Check volume:**

- Ringer volume must be up (not just media volume)
- Use volume buttons on side of phone

## Step 11: Safety and Privacy


**Protecting Yourself with Text Messages:**


**Recognizing Scam Texts:**


**Common scam texts claim:**

- Package delivery problem (asking to click link)
- Bank account issue (asking for info or to click link)
- Prize or refund (too good to be true)
- Family emergency (asking for money)

**Red flags:**

- Unsolicited texts about accounts or deliveries
- Urgent language ("Act now!" "Account will close!")
- Requests for personal info (SSN, passwords, bank details)
- Suspicious links (shortened URLs, misspelled domains)
- Requests for payment via gift cards

**What to do:**

- **Don't click links** in suspicious texts
- **Don't reply**
- **Delete the text**
- **Block the number**
- Forward to 7726 (SPAM) to report to carrier

**See our "Recognizing Text Message Scams" guide for comprehensive coverage.**


**Never Share Via Text:**


**Never send via text message:**

- Social Security Number
- Credit card numbers
- Bank account numbers
- Passwords or PINs
- Photos of driver's license or ID

**Why:** Text messages are not encrypted (can be intercepted). Use secure methods for sensitive info.


**Protecting Privacy:**


**Lock screen preview:**

- Message previews appear on lock screen (anyone can read)
- To disable:
    - iPhone: Settings → Notifications → Messages → Show Previews → Never or When Unlocked
    - Android: Settings → Apps → Messages → Notifications → Sensitive notifications → Hide

**Message backup:**

- iCloud backs up messages (iPhone)
- Google backs up messages (Android)
- Someone with access to your cloud account can read messages
- Secure your account with strong password and two-factor authentication

**Deleting Sensitive Conversations:**


**For privacy, delete conversations containing:**

- Personal information
- Financial details
- Private photos
- Anything you wouldn't want discovered if phone lost/stolen

**Texting While Driving:**


**Never text and drive:**

- Illegal in most places
- Extremely dangerous (reaction time severely impaired)
- Can wait—no text is worth a crash

**Safe alternatives:**

- Pull over to text
- Use voice-to-text (hands-free)
- Let passenger text for you
- Enable Do Not Disturb While Driving (iPhone: Settings → Focus → Driving)

## Quick Reference: Texting Basics At-a-Glance


**Sending a Text:**

1. Open Messages app
2. Tap New Message (+)
3. Enter recipient's name or number
4. Type message
5. Tap Send

**Replying to a Text:**

1. Tap notification OR open Messages app
2. Tap conversation
3. Type reply in text field
4. Tap Send

**Sending a Photo:**

1. Open conversation
2. Tap camera icon
3. Take photo OR choose from gallery
4. Tap Send

**Deleting a Conversation:**

1. Conversation list
2. Swipe left (iPhone) or long-press (Android)
3. Tap Delete

**Blocking a Number:**

1. Open conversation
2. Tap number/name at top
3. Block this Caller (iPhone) or Block (Android)

**Common Emoji:**

- 😊 Happy
- 👍 Thumbs up
- ❤️ Love
- 😂 Laughing
- 🙏 Thank you

**Key Principles:**


**Texting is simpler than it seems:** Open app, type, send. That's the core. Everything else is optional features that enhance the experience but aren't necessary to get started.


**There's no "right" way to text:** Some people use emoji extensively, others never use them. Some people use abbreviations, others type full words. Some respond instantly, others take hours. All approaches are valid—text in whatever style feels comfortable to you.


**Mistakes don't matter:** Typos, autocorrect errors, accidental sends—they're all common and understood. Text messaging is informal communication. Nobody expects perfection.


**You control the pace:** Unlike phone calls (which demand immediate attention), texts are asynchronous. You read and respond when convenient. Don't feel pressured to reply instantly or engage in conversations you don't want.


**Practice builds confidence:** Your first few texts may feel awkward or slow. This is completely normal. Within days, it becomes automatic. Send a few practice texts to patient family members or friends. Tell them you're learning—they'll be happy to help.


**Texting enhances relationships:** Quick check-ins, sharing moments through photos, coordinating plans—text messaging keeps you connected to people you care about with minimal effort. It's one of the most valuable communication tools ever created, and now you know how to use it.

- [ ] Remember: Everyone started as a beginner; you're doing great

**Texting is now the primary way billions of people communicate daily. You've just joined them. Welcome to easier, more convenient connection with everyone you care about.** 📱💬
